newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana House committee approves $12 Bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana House committee approves $12 Bln budget.

text.p: Louisiana's House Appropriations Committee approved a $12 billion budget that does not rely on the renewal of $110 million in sales taxes.
The committee's proposal uses $363.2 million of surplus funds from fiscal 1996 plus some excess revenues from this year to pay off state pension system debt early over seven years.
That would free up money that would otherwise go toward debt service for teacher raises and education and health programs.
Gov. Mike Foster had sought renewal of a one-cent sales tax on food and utilities that expires June 30. Lawmakers will consider the renewal in a special session later this month.
In his budget plan, Foster tied the tax renewal to $65 million of teacher pay raises.
House Appropriations Committee Chairman Rep. Jerry Luke LeBlanc, D-Lafayette, said the committee's budget is balanced without renwal of the tax, and still provides $65.2 million for teacher raises.

If the tax is renewed, the committee plan would allocate an additional $65 million for teacher raises, $30 million for reading programs and special classes at public schools and $15 million for higher education.
Foster also proposed retiring pension system debt early, but would use the savings to fund capital projects. The committee plan would rely on surplus in fiscal 1997 and 1998 to fund those projects.
The committee also approved a proposal to raise Louisiana's homestead tax exemption to $100,000 from $75,000.
The proposal now goes to the full House.
